summary:
Build succeeds. All four checks (typecheck, lint, test, build) pass.

Root cause: `src/services/http.js` excluded every path under `/auth/` from the silent refresh-and-retry on a 401, instead of only the two paths that genuinely need to skip it (`/auth/login`, which has no token to refresh; `/auth/refresh` itself, to avoid a loop). That meant an expired access token on `/auth/me` (used during session restore) or `/auth/change-password` failed immediately instead of transparently refreshing — i.e. refresh-token-based recovery silently didn't apply to those calls while it worked everywhere else, matching the reported "access token only working, refresh flow not working" symptom.

Fix: replaced the `path.startsWith('/auth/')` prefix check with an exact-match exclusion set (`/auth/login`, `/auth/refresh`), so all other authenticated endpoints — including the `/auth/*` ones — get the same refresh-and-retry treatment. Added `src/services/http.test.js` covering: refresh+retry on a normal endpoint, refresh+retry on an authenticated `/auth/*` endpoint, and no infinite loop when the refresh call itself 401s.
blockers: Visual verification failed: The entire app (including /login and the root route) renders a blank white page in the dev server — the frontend throws at startup due to a missing VITE_API_BASE_URL env var, so no UI (including login/token-refresh behavior) can be visually verified.

visual_check.evidence: The entire app (including /login and the root route) renders a blank white page in the dev server — the frontend throws at startup due to a missing VITE_API_BASE_URL env var, so no UI (including login/token-refresh behavior) can be visually verified.

endpoints.purpose: Exchange the httpOnly refresh cookie for a new access token

context_sharing.notes: This module authenticates via `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` plus an httpOnly refresh cookie (credentials: 'include'), with silent refresh-and-retry on 401, not via X-User-Role/X-User-Id headers as described elsewhere in this repo's conventions — that is a mismatch the other side must account for. Error bodies are shaped as { error: string, details: string[] }. No endpoints under /api/v1/* are implemented in these two files themselves; /api/v1/contracts appears only as a literal path string in a test mock and is not evidence of a real contract.
